newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Optus says pay TV is an attractive business.
newsitem.headline: Optus says pay TV is an attractive business.

text.p: Optus Communications Pty Ltd chief executive officer Zygmunt Switkowski said on Tuesday that pay television was an attractive business despite the A$330 million in losses by its Optus Vision unit.
"Pay TV is turning out to be a surprisingly attractive business as we have got to know it better," Switkowski told reporters after giving a speech to the Australian Telephone Users Group (ATUG).
Optus Vision, which also provides local telephony and online interactive services, has about 185,000 pay TV subscribers.

"In an industry that is poorly designed our part is probably the most robust and after spending a month looking into the fine details of the business we are very reassured that it really looks like a nifty business," Switkowski said.
Australia's pay television industry has made losses of about A$1.5 billion since its started in 1993.
The other main players include Australis Media Ltd and Foxtel, which is owned by News Corp Ltd and the state-owned Telstra Corp.
